title: AMD's record quarter: Data center business doubles, while gaming craters
gist: AMD posted record Q3 revenue of $13.4 billion (+45% YoY) as data center revenue rose 97% to $8.5 billion on EPYC CPUs and Instinct MI450 GPUs, while gaming fell 40% to $773 million on the console cycle. Q4 guidance of about $17 billion (+66% YoY) would put AMD above Intel's $15-16 billion guidance for the first time, and MI455X Helios racks are shipping in volume to Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle.

insights.claim: AMD reported record Q3 2026 revenue of $13.4 billion, up 45% year over year.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Confirms AMD's accelerating growth driven by AI data center demand.
insights.locator: AMD reported third-quarter revenues on Tuesday

insights.claim: CFO Jean Hu guided Q4 revenue to about $17 billion plus or minus 3%, roughly 66% year-over-year growth and 27% above Q3, driven primarily by data center acceleration.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Sharp sequential acceleration implies a steep MI455X/Helios ramp into year-end.
insights.quote: The middle point of our guidance represents approximately 66% year-over-year revenue growth

insights.claim: With Intel guiding Q4 revenue to $15-16 billion per Tom's Hardware, AMD would exceed Intel's quarterly revenue for the first time in history if both hit guidance.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: A symbolic shift in x86 and semiconductor leadership that could re-rate relative valuations.

insights.claim: AMD's data center segment rose 97% year over year to a record $8.5 billion on EPYC server CPU demand and the Instinct MI450 GPU launch, with operating margin expanding from 25% to 34% and operating income up 168% to $2.88 billion.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Operating leverage in data center shows AI GPU scale is translating into profit, not just revenue.
insights.locator: The data center segment of AMD’s

insights.claim: CEO Lisa Su said AMD began shipping MI455X in volume during the quarter and lead customers Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle quickly brought their first Helios racks online.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Broad hyperscaler and frontier-lab adoption of AMD rack-scale systems strengthens its position as a credible Nvidia alternative.
insights.quote: started shipping MI455X in volume in the quarter, and lead customers, including Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Oracle, brought their first Helios racks online quickly

insights.claim: AMD gaming revenue fell 40% year over year to $773 million due to lower semi-custom console chip and graphics sales, which Lisa Su attributed to the expected stage of the console cycle.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Gaming is now a shrinking, cyclical sliver of AMD and largely irrelevant to the investment case.

insights.claim: AMD's client segment grew 7% to $2.95 billion led by Ryzen mobile chips, while embedded revenue rose 29% to $1.1 billion on aerospace and defense, automotive, communications and industrial demand.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Embedded is recovering strongly while client PCs grow modestly, diversifying beyond data center.
